assumptions: The continuous computation of wheel slip, PID control, and plant dynamics is outside this discrete FSM; the DSL models `slp` as the supervisor input used by the specified threshold guards.
The initial state is `increase` because it is the first state named in the NL state list and no alternative initial state is specified.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: first empty cycle dispatches the initial transition to increase and asserts inlet-valve command outputs.
scenario_results.name: default_init_enters_increase

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: increase must transition to hold exactly at slp=0.01 and neutralize both valves.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire probe: increase must stay increase when slp is just above 0.01.
scenario_results.name: increase_no_hold_above_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: hold must transition to increase only when slp is greater than 0.01 and set increase outputs.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire boundary probe: hold must not transition to increase at slp=0.01 because that guard is strict greater-than.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_increase_at_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: hold must transition to decrease when slp is below -0.01 and command pressure release.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire boundary probe: hold must not transition to decrease at slp=-0.01 because that guard is strict less-than.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_decrease_at_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: decrease must transition back to hold exactly at slp=-0.01 and neutralize valves and pump.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire probe: decrease must stay decrease when slp remains below -0.01.
scenario_results.name: decrease_no_hold_below_lower_boundary

evidence: NL: states `increase`, `hold`, and `decrease` with actions `k1`, `k2`, `n`.
DSL: state increase/hold/decrease each has matching enter assignments.
DSL: transitions match `slp <= 0.01`, `slp > 0.01`, `slp < -0.01`, and `slp >= -0.01`.
sim_summary: 9/9 scenarios passed, including boundary and no-fire cases.
findings.summary: The DSL covers the explicitly specified three-state hydraulic supervisor: increase, hold, decrease, their valve/pump entry actions, and the four slip-error threshold transitions.

evidence: NL: `Wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute the slip ratio, and the PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor`.
DSL: only declares `slp`, `k1`, `k2`, and `n`; no wheel speed, vehicle speed, slip-ratio computation, PID state, PID gains, or continuous plant dynamics are represented.
GroundingMap assumption: `continuous computation of wheel slip, PID control, and plant dynamics is outside this discrete FSM; the DSL models slp as the supervisor input`.
findings.summary: The broader PID/slip computation context is not modeled; this is acceptable only if the intended scope is the discrete supervisor with `slp` as an external input.

evidence: NL specifies the three states and transition guards but does not explicitly state the initial state.
DSL: `[*] -> increase;`.
GroundingMap assumption: `The initial state is increase because it is the first state named in the NL state list and no alternative initial state is specified.`
findings.summary: The initial transition to `increase` is an assumption rather than a directly stated NL requirement.

evidence: DSL: `slp` is declared as `def float slp = 0.0` and is read by guards but never written.
design_diagnostics_summary: `nl_external_input_vars` includes `slp` with external-input role evidence.
DSL: `k1`, `k2`, and `n` are outputs set by entry actions and are not expected to affect transition guards.
diagnostics: W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for `slp`; W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for `k1`, `k2`, and `n`; all are advisory with blocking_count 0.
findings.summary: The model uses ordinary variables for both external input and actuator outputs, which triggers advisory diagnostics but does not invalidate the supervisor mapping.

evidence: sim_summary scenario `default_init_enters_increase` asserts initial transition to increase.
NL does not explicitly require initial state `increase`.
Boundary scenarios otherwise align with explicit NL guard requirements.
findings.summary: The simulation oracle strongly checks the FSM thresholds and outputs but also validates the ungrounded initial-state assumption.

evidence: GroundingMap has required elements for all three states, entry actions, four transitions, and four guards with high confidence.
GroundingMap source_summary lists the initial state as an assumption derived from the first named state.
findings.summary: Grounding is strong for states, actions, variables, and guards, but the initial-state grounding relies on an assumption rather than direct source evidence.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary: 3 leaf states, 5 transitions including initial, 4 variables, 3 actions.
design_diagnostics_summary: ok=true, blocking_count=0.
sim_summary: ok=true, 9/9 scenarios passed.

findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate for the discrete supervisor scope. No quality cap is warranted unless the review target requires modeling the full PID/slip/plant coupling.
